accuracy.evidence: Shape and measure language checked against Development Matters 2021 for 3-4 year olds (talk about 2D and 3D shapes with flat, round, straight, sides, corners; select shapes for a purpose such as flat surfaces for building; combine shapes to make an arch; compare size and length; understand position through words). The stability rule in the lab is the real one: a block stays while its centre of mass is over the block below (offset up to half its width), and the plank must be strictly longer than the gap to bear on both supports.

misconceptions.evidence: Wrong moves are the ones seen in block play: balancing a ball, putting a cone mid-tower, starting with a small block, pushing blocks off-centre, choosing a plank exactly as long as the gap (it falls in) and building unequal pillars so the plank slopes, plus pillars lower than the car.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtower is a building simulation with five drawn 3D shapes, a size-ordered stacking tower, a draggable block with a centre line that tips when its middle passes the edge, three plank lengths over a gap, and pillar heights checked against a car and a bus. flagfit (shapes into holes) and flagheavy (heavy and light) share no mechanism; the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each rule by trying: the ball rolls off and the message says it is round all over, a big block placed late wobbles red on the small one, a block dragged off-centre tips as soon as the dotted middle line misses the block, the 2-long plank drops into a 2-wide gap, and the bus bumps until both pillars reach 3.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers: Yes for a ball staying on a cube, The smallest for the bottom block, and Yes for a plank just as long as the gap. The task straight after tests each guess and the done message says whether it held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with ten tagged wrong answers, each naming the slip: ball round all over, cone pointy, small at the bottom tips, blocks pushed past the edge, a plank the same as the gap, a plank shorter than the gap, pillars lower than the car, unequal pillars, and cube or long block chosen as top-only.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK 0.1 against the family limit of 5.0, with one-syllable words and an action in every sentence. Adult text scores FK 8.3 against 10 and uses the terms 2D and 3D shape, face, flat and curved surface, sphere, cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, prism, arch, centre of mass, span, support and positional language.

no_filler.evidence: No stock phrases; the filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph is one building rule with a concrete example; adult paragraphs give the curriculum, the maths under the play, named mistakes and what the lab does. Overlap with every other lesson is under 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark (steps 1, 4 and 5) show shelf shapes in 64 px wide tap zones with labels, towers and pillars clear of the shelf, and the car beside the bridge with nothing clipped. Pointer drags on the iPhone viewport dropped the tube and cube on the tower, rolled the ball off, dropped the 2-long plank into the gap and tipped an off-centre block.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe run found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop or iPhone, and no console errors. Every canvas action has a labelled button (Put the ball on the tower, Move the block left, Drop the block, Try the plank 4 blocks long, Add a block to the left pillar, Drive under the bridge), and the canvas aria-label reads each result aloud.
